title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. ~757-759 of the sequel to the Longue Marche, section '4°: Lie approximation of (Π_0, 𝔊_0, M)'). Start with a discrete LT-group 𝔊_0 and a normal L-subgroup Π_0. Π_0 is a surface group with its lacets, i.e. its cusp/inertia generators. Grothendieck assumes the multiplier character 𝔊_0 → {±1} given by the action on the lacets of Π_0 is trivial. He gives a Q-group scheme 𝔊_Q and a homomorphism φ: 𝔊_0 → 𝔊(Q) (65). Two conditions are imposed. (i) For each structural homomorphism K_i: T_0 (≅ Z) → 𝔊_0 (66), the composite with φ is quasi-unipotent. (ii) 𝔊_Q is generated by φ(𝔊_0).

This page. The K_i then extend to outer homomorphisms K̲_i: T̲_{0,Q} → 𝔊_Q (67). Here T̲_{0,Q} is essentially G_a, the unipotent hull of Z. The square (68) commutes: T_0 → T̲_0(Q) canonical, then K̲_i(Q), equals φ∘K_i.

He then defines a (possibly infinite-dimensional) Q-group scheme M^φ_Q. It parametrizes pairs (u, μ) with u ∈ Aut(𝔊_Q) and μ ∈ G_m. The condition is that for each i, fpqc-locally there is a section f_i of Π̲_Q (the Zariski closure of φ(Π_0)) with u(K̲_i(λ)) = int(f_i)^{-1}(K̲_i(μλ)) (69). In words, u sends each lacet to a Π-conjugate of its μ-th power. This is the algebraic analogue of the cyclotomic action of Galois on inertia, λ ↦ λ^{χ(σ)}.

There is an augmentation χ: M^φ_Q → G_{m,Q}, (u, μ) ↦ μ. Inner automorphisms by 𝔊_Q land in M^φ_Q with μ = 1, because multipliers are trivial and 𝔊_0 preserves the Π-conjugacy classes of lacets. So χ kills Im(𝔊_Q → M^φ_Q) and factors through Γ^φ_Q := M^φ_Q / Im 𝔊_Q → G_m via χ_Γ (70).

The page ends by starting the comparison: if (𝔊_0, Π_0) sits in a Teichmüller system (Π ⊂ 𝔊 ⊂ M), the next page gets M_Q → M^φ_Q. If 𝔊_Q is centreless, 𝔊_Q ⊂ M^φ_Q is a universal extension relative to φ.

Purpose: build a Q-pro-algebraic (Malcev-type, relative to φ) model of the Teichmüller system and of its 'Galois' quotient Γ, carrying an algebraic cyclotomic character. In other words, an algebraic substitute for the profinite group M/𝔊 acting on the tower.
errors: Aut(𝔊_Q) is generally not representable by an algebraic group when 𝔊_Q is infinite-dimensional. Grothendieck's marginal '(inf. dim)' acknowledges this; representability of the subfunctor defined by the locally-existential condition (69) is not addressed.

That Im 𝔊_Q lies in M^φ_Q (needed for (70)) requires 𝔊_0 to preserve each lacet class up to Π-conjugacy, with trivial multiplier, and these properties to pass to the Zariski closure. This is implicit (via the hypothesis on the previous page) but not stated on this page.

'μλ' presupposes T̲_{0,Q} ≅ G_a, i.e. a unipotent image. For merely quasi-unipotent K_i, the hull of Z may have a finite component, on which scaling by μ ∈ G_m is not defined; this subtlety is not treated.
Normality of Im 𝔊_Q in M^φ_Q is used but not argued. It is true: u∘int(g)∘u^{-1} = int(u(g)).

ideas.what: Q-algebraic 'Lie approximation' of a discrete Teichmüller-type group relative to a homomorphism into a Q-group with quasi-unipotent inertia
ideas.modern_name: relative (weighted) Malcev completion of mapping class / fundamental groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (relative completion idea), Hain (1990s), Hain–Matsumoto (weighted completion, 2003)
ideas.where_published: Ideas of 'Lie' approximations are hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme; this specific construction appears unpublished

ideas.what: Group scheme of pairs (u, μ) ∈ Aut(𝔊_Q) × G_m sending each lacet to a Π-conjugate of its μ-th power
ideas.modern_name: pro-algebraic Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group GT(Q) (inertia-preserving automorphisms with multiplier λ ∈ k*)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara; inertia-preserving outer automorphisms: Ihara, Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto
ideas.where_published: Profinite analogue implicit in Esquisse / Longue Marche (1981); the Q-algebraic version not published

ideas.what: Quotient Γ^φ_Q = M^φ_Q / Im 𝔊_Q with an algebraic cyclotomic character χ_Γ to G_m
ideas.modern_name: algebraic analogue of the outer Galois action with cyclotomic character (cf. GT(k) → k*, motivic Galois group → G_m)

missed.claim: Grothendieck defines, around 1981, a Q-pro-algebraic group of automorphisms of the completed Teichmüller group. These are constrained to send each lacet to a Π-conjugate of its μ-th power, μ ∈ G_m, with a character to G_m. This is formally the same shape as Drinfeld's GT(k) of 1990: pairs (λ, f), σ(x) = x^λ, σ(y) = f^{-1} y^λ f. It is also the shape of Hain–Matsumoto's relative-completion treatment of Galois actions on mapping class groups. Grothendieck frames it in his 'Teichmüller system' language for the whole tower.
missed.quote: le schéma en groupes (inf/dim) sur Q des couples (automorphismes de 𝔊_Q, et d'un μ ∈ 𝔾_m), tels que pour tout i ∈ I, il existe loc. une section f_i de Π_Q ... u(K_i(λ)) = int(f_i)^{-1}(μλ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents that Grothendieck anticipated not only profinite GT but its pro-algebraic (Malcev / relative completion) version with G_m-multiplier. That is relevant to the history of GT(Q), GRT and motivic approaches to Galois actions on moduli towers. His 'universal extension relative to φ' (next page) may suggest a functorial definition not exactly matching the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: A clear, carefully set-up Q-algebraic analogue of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group with multiplier character, predating Drinfeld and Hain–Matsumoto, in a little-studied portion of the Longue Marche sequel. The core ideas (Malcev completion, inertia-preserving automorphisms) are now standard, and his anticipation of GT is generally known, so the surprise is moderate.
transcription_corrections: 'μ ∈ Γ_m' should read 'μ ∈ 𝔾_m' (multiplicative group); the handwriting shows G_m.
'(inf/dim)' is the marginal insertion '(inf. dim)', i.e. infinite-dimensional group scheme.
In (69), the right-hand side should read int(f_i)^{-1}(K_i(μλ)); the handwriting abbreviates it as int(f_i)^{-1}(μλ).
The groups denoted 𝔊 are Grothendieck's script G (Teichmüller-type group), consistent with the neighbouring pages.
